name: Morse.IsUnbrokenGeodesic
hypotheses: c 0 in N and c 1 in N (e.g. c in Omega), with V and Z finite-dimensional (the standing setting); the direction blind => project needs no hypothesis
difference: The project asks c in N and c'' normal to N only on the open interval (0,1) (IsGeodesicOn on Ioo 0 1), the blind definition on all of [0,1]. Off Omega an end point may leave N: N = (0, infty) in R, c = id is a project unbroken geodesic but not a blind one (c 0 = 0 not in N). With the end points in N the end-point normality follows by continuity.
why: Both require c C^infty on [0,1]. On (0,1) the second derivative within [0,1] is deriv (deriv c) and the blind tangent space (span of velocities) is Morse.tangentSubspace (tangentSpace_eq, copied from item Morse_tangentSubspace), so blind => project. Conversely, with c 0, c 1 in N, t -> P_{c(t)}(c''(t)) is continuous on [0,1] (Morse.ContDiffOn.prj_comp) and zero on (0,1), hence zero on the closure [0,1]; that is the blind normality at the end points.
